# Source-Bound Native Zero-MTP CustomJoint Reduction

Issue #12176 admits a separate, derived OpenSim mechanical artifact from the
assembled 557-muscle BUET–Hamner source. The actual bilateral MTP joints in
that source are one-coordinate **CustomJoints**. The pre-existing PinJoint
reducer remains restricted to PinJoints; this exact CustomJoint profile shares
the #12167 zero-transform admission and native comparison, without changing
the source model or treating a joint-class name as sufficient evidence.

## Declared Source and Reduction Domain

The request binds the source XML SHA-256, a fresh derived output, and ordered
zero-radian targets for `mtp_angle_r` and `mtp_angle_l`. The two source joints
must each contain exactly that coordinate, with a `rotation1` LinearFunction
of coefficients $(1,0)$ and five coordinate-free Constant$(0)$ axes. Their
native default and achieved values and speeds must be zero, locked but not
prescribed, and strictly interior to any clamped range. Their native parent
and child frames must coincide at the achieved zero target. Source XML is
scanned for any consumer of the removed coordinate names outside the target
joints. Unexpected consumers, XML entities, altered laws, nonzero or unlocked
targets, stale source bytes, and an occupied output path reject before or
during the derived copy's admission. The exact profile wrapper and shared
admission module are separately hashed.

After a native whole-joint-to-weld operation on a copy, the result is serialized
and freshly loaded. Bodies, muscles, actuators, constraints, all unrelated
joints and their native property dumps must remain unchanged. Common named
continuous values are restored exactly; `initSystem` can assemble before that
restoration, but no subsequent assembly, fiber equilibrium or integration is
used as an equivalence shortcut.

## Sampled Native Mechanical Comparison

At initialized, right-ankle, right-knee and pelvis-tilt common poses where
valid, native unit-speed probes construct source and derived mobility maps.
The rank-complete lift $L$ must preserve body transforms/velocities, all 557
muscle path lengths and native lengthening speeds, native constraint position
and velocity residuals, and

$$M_d=L^\mathsf{T}M_sL,\qquad
f_d=L^\mathsf{T}f_s,\qquad
f=J_{\mathrm{system}}^\mathsf{T}F_{\mathrm{body}}+f_{\mathrm{mobility}}.$$

All observations must be finite. The fixture tolerance is $10^{-10}$ in each
quantity's native units; the aggregate is not a normalized physiological
error. Applied force excludes inertial bias and constraint reactions.

The qualified OpenSim `4.6-2026-06-22-85aaf64` experiment first reduced the
unchanged assembled v4 XML SHA-256
`8d4d349747060efbac31c707c4e01f452746a8fba32be77a425b5ac5be1d34a3`
and then reduced the retained abdomen→subtalar artifact SHA-256
`8d8c3cf1dbe5e149df07b0309d508d78d2524e3c7beeaee327e24c4c43c8b81b`.
The latter produced a fresh 2,247,450-byte XML SHA-256
`453e09c4e42dcc3f4b74a3b2efeff063e96c3820b3eee1efe95eef249579010d`,
with rank 56, condition one and zero differences in every measured quantity
at four sampled poses. The source-bound public receipt and turnover contain
the final module, script and native-binary identities.

An independent root-run composition receipt
`composed_reduction_12161_v2/receipt.json` (SHA-256
`c82e77aa1a760e6965a45cee22be530bab67fb8ed71de710521b51f9c7f3b5d7`)
binds these reducer bytes and compares the unchanged original against all
three derived reductions at three complete, coupled prepared states. Its
rank-56 lift and eight mechanical error classes are zero at those states;
`MocoStudy.initCasADiSolver` succeeds. The prior PinJoint-class failure is
retained separately. Initialization is not a solve or tracking result.

This is a sampled continuous-state mechanical prerequisite. It does not prove
complete SimTK restart, all-pose force/power equivalence, physiological
muscle-state suitability, missing visual-resource closure, contact/grip,
Moco solve, muscle-only captured-swing matching or fresh full-horizon
excitation replay.
All 17 variants and six engine families remain in the epic denominator.
